newsitem.title: USA: Gale warnings as Josephine races up US East Coast.
newsitem.headline: Gale warnings as Josephine races up US East Coast.

text.p: Gale warnings were in effect along the U.S. East Coast from Savannah, Ga., into New England Tuesday as the remains of Tropical Storm Josephine, considered an extratropical system but still bearing strong winds and rains, raced north, National Hurricane Center said.
A gale warning also was in effect for southern Florida from Jupiter Inlet south through the Florida Keys.

At 1100 EDT/1500 GMT, Josephine's center was near latitude 35.5 north and longitude 77.5 west or near Kinston, North Carolina, and moving northeast near 40 mph (64 kph). That motion was expected to continue Tuesday, putting Josephine's center near the New Jersey coast Tuesday evening and near southeastern New England Tuesday night.

Maximum sustained winds were near 50 mph (80 kph) and little change in strength was likely during the next 24 hours. Tropical storm force winds extended outward up to 405 miles (648 km) from Josephine's center, mostly over water.

Rainfall of five inches (12.5 cm) was expected along the storm's path and there was a threat of isolated tornadoes over northeastern North Carolina, extreme southeastern Virginia and eastern Maryland for the next few hours.
